summary:
No Sivas-specific statute, enforcement programme, incident or institution concerning transgender visitors is documented in the sources assembled for this edition. The province of Sivas stands under the national framework of Türkiye, and no local authority in Sivas is recorded adding prohibitions of its own.

That national framework is set out in the sources as follows. Homosexuality has not been a criminal offence in Turkey since the Ottoman penal code of 1858, and transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988, subject to sex reassignment surgery, medical examination and court permission. There is no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity.

Openly LGBTQ people are barred from serving in the Turkish military: a health regulation defines homosexuality as a 'psychosexual illness', conscripts who declare it must provide photographic proof, and the resulting 'unfit report' can leak and fuel later discrimination in public life. Same-sex marriage, civil unions and domestic partnerships are not recognised. When the 12th judicial reform package passed in 2026 the anti-LGBTQ provisions were removed from the bill, leaving only symbolic same-sex weddings possible.

Since 2015 authorities have banned Pride events in Istanbul and other cities in most years, with police using tear gas, water cannons and mass detentions against participants who defied the bans. In June 2025 authorities issued blanket bans against the LGBTI and Trans pride marches in Istanbul, police subjected peaceful protesters to unlawful use of force and over 90 people were arbitrarily detained; three activists were remanded in prison on 29 June 2025 under Law No. 2911 and released on 8 August pending trial, while prosecutions of 92 people for participating in pride marches continued at year's end. Blanket bans plus case-by-case prosecutions under Law No. 2911 form the enforcement climate applying to provincial authorities in Sivas as across Turkey.

In December 2025 an İzmir court ordered the dissolution of the Young LGBTI+ Association, ruling that it had shared 'obscene' images incompatible with 'society's moral values' that could 'encourage or promote' LGBTI identities. Early-2026 press reports record that the government considered legislation criminalising public advocacy of 'behaviour contrary to biological sex'. Turkey placed 47th of 49 countries in ILGA-Europe's 2026 Rainbow Europe ranking.
tangentialFactors:
The national ranking of 47th of 49 in ILGA-Europe's 2026 Rainbow Europe index places Turkey near the bottom of the European comparison set, though the index measures legal framework rather than street-level risk in any one province.

The enforcement pattern documented in Istanbul and İzmir — blanket march bans, mass detentions under Law No. 2911, and court-ordered dissolution of an LGBTI+ association — is described in the sources as applying to provincial authorities generally, including Sivas, rather than as an Istanbul-only practice.

Transgender residents of Sivas can change their legal gender under the national rules in force since 1988, which require sex reassignment surgery, medical examination and court permission.

Residents have no comprehensive statutory protection against discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity, and no recognition of same-sex marriage, civil unions or domestic partnerships.

LGBTQ residents are barred from open military service under a health regulation treating homosexuality as a 'psychosexual illness'; the resulting unfit report can leak and affect later employment and public life.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the draft legislative package reported by Human Rights Watch on 29 October 2025 has since been enacted, and whether the early-2026 reported proposals on public advocacy have advanced, is unresolved in the sources.

No source in this inventory documents Sivas-specific policing, detention, facility access or local government practice toward transgender visitors or residents; the assessment rests on the national framework.
